fluff.overview: The Riga II-class destroyer-carrier was designed and built by Boeing Interstellar at their New Earth facilities, entering service with the Star League Defense Force in 2747. A successor to the earlier Riga-class frigate, the Riga II was reclassified from frigate to destroyer and escort carrier, filling a critical gap in the SLDF order of battle for fast, heavily armed escorts capable of screening the fleet's most valuable capital WarShips. Boeing Interstellar, already well regarded for their earlier naval work including the original Riga, delivered a design that combined formidable striking power with extensive carrier capacity and exceptional strategic mobility. The class earned a reputation within the SLDF as one of its premier escort platforms, prized for its ability to protect high-priority fleet elements during both routine patrol operations and sustained fleet actions far from friendly supply lines.
fluff.capabilities:
At 600,000 tons and 630 meters, the Riga II is a heavy destroyer-carrier built around speed and striking power. Four medium naval PPCs and two NAC/40 naval autocannons in the nose deliver punishing alpha strikes at close range. The forward and aft quarters each mount paired NL45 and NL35 naval lasers for sustained damage across multiple arcs. Twin NAC/30 naval autocannons in each broadside provide flanking firepower. The stern is defended by a formidable battery of four NL45 and four NL35 naval lasers, discouraging pursuit. Five hundred eighty-one double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal load.

Six hundred four tons of lamellor ferro-carbide armor provide heavy protection, though this allocation was considered modest for a vessel of its tonnage, a trade-off driven by the need to accommodate the extensive weapons suite. A lithium-fusion battery enables rapid successive jumps, making the Riga II one of the most strategically mobile WarShips of its era. Thirty-six aerospace fighters across two bays and five small craft provide extensive carrier capability, justifying the destroyer-carrier classification. Two docking collars accommodate attached DropShips. Two gravity decks measuring 140 and 65 meters in diameter serve the crew of over three hundred, and a cavernous cargo hold of over 70,000 tons supports extended independent deployments.
fluff.deployment: No individual Riga II-class vessels are recorded by name in published sources. The class served exclusively with the Star League Defense Force as heavy escorts, typically assigned to formations protecting the fleet's heaviest combatants. Their combination of carrier capacity and strategic mobility made them particularly effective as rapid-response assets, able to reach developing situations faster than most vessels of comparable firepower. Fleet commanders also valued the Riga II for independent patrols, given its fighter complement and substantial cargo capacity, which allowed extended operations without frequent resupply.
fluff.history:
The Riga II-class destroyer-carrier was born from crisis. When First Lord Simon Cameron was assassinated in 2747, the Star League Defense Force recognized an urgent need for heavy escorts to accompany its most valuable fleet elements. Boeing Interstellar on New Earth, the same firm that had produced the original Riga-class frigate, received the contract. The resulting WarShip gave the SLDF a fast, capable escort with the strategic mobility to keep pace with even the highest-priority fleet formations.

Production was rapid. Sixty Riga IIs had been commissioned by Christmas of 2766, and the class became regarded as too valuable to risk in situations where lesser vessels could serve. This paradox defined much of the class's operational life. During the Periphery uprisings that followed the Amaris Coup, Riga IIs frequently served as first responders, their speed allowing rapid deployment to trouble spots. Periphery navies, unable to face the SLDF directly, targeted more exposed vessels and largely avoided engaging the fast-moving destroyer-carriers, paradoxically keeping them safer than many frontline combatants.

The campaign to liberate the Terran Hegemony from Stefan Amaris proved far more costly. Two Riga IIs assigned to the First Fleet were destroyed by the Reagan Space Defense System while engaging surface targets over Geneva. In the broader liberation campaign, the class's speed made it essential for engaging Caspar drone WarShips, and Riga IIs found themselves in the vanguard of multiple offensives alongside McKenna and Luxor-class vessels. Half of the remaining Riga IIs were lost during the campaign, though this was still better than the ninety percent loss rate suffered by Lola III and Essex II-class destroyers. After the fighting, four badly damaged survivors were stripped and scuttled.

The remaining twenty-two Riga IIs departed with General Kerensky's Exodus fleet. In exile, they served as primary patrol units on the Pentagon worlds. When Nicholas Kerensky departed for Strana Mechty in December 2801, most were caught up in the devastating civil wars that followed. Two survivors were destroyed during Operation Klondike. The six remaining vessels served the nascent Clans for another century before undergoing extensive refits around 2947 that transformed them into the York-class destroyer-carrier, ending the Riga II designation but carrying its legacy forward into Clan naval service.
